evidence.curator_note: SUBSTRATE IDENTIFIED BY THE TEXT, NOT GUESSED: the facing page (p. 220) ends '... Loss of NO may also occur from aromatic EE+ ions, such as protonated nitrobenzene (Crombie and Harrison 1988; Equation 8.124).' The drawing matches: a benzene ring bonded to N, the N carrying a doubly bonded O below it and, up to the right, an O drawn with '+' above it and an H, i.e. protonated nitrobenzene written in the pentavalent-nitrogen form C6H5-N(=O)=O(+)H. The arrow is labelled 'r Ph' (rearrangement by phenyl migration) and the product it points to is protonated phenyl nitrite: the ring now bonded to an O that carries '+', an H below it and -NO to its right. ARC COUNT (convention D): Book draws 1 arc, and it is FULL-barbed (a solid triangular head, hence a two-electron arrow): a short straight arrow whose tail sits on the C(ipso)-N bond and whose head points up and to the right, at the +OH oxygen. That single drawn arc is the migration itself. Move <2> is the one that corresponds to it (the C-N bonding pair leaving the C-N bond); move <1> is IMPLICIT and not drawn on the page. HONEST NOTE ON WHY THE ENCODING IS NOT A LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION OF THAT ONE ARC: read literally as 'C-N pair -> C-O bond', the drawn arc is not electron-balanced in the charge-separated Lewis structure RDKit requires - it would leave nitrogen at formal +2 and oxygen at -1. In the book's own pentavalent-nitrogen drawing the arc does balance, but only because a second, undrawn arc is implied there too (the N=O(+)H pi pair dropping onto nitrogen). The encoding used here keeps both bond changes explicit: an oxygen lone pair forms the new C-O bond (move <1>) while the C-N bonding pair becomes a nitrogen lone pair (move <2>), which is the same net 1,2-aryl shift. LOCALIZATION (conventions B/C): the book puts '+' on the hydroxyl oxygen and draws nitrogen with five bonds; RDKit rejects a neutral pentavalent nitrogen and silently renormalizes any attempt at it into [N+](=[OH+])[O-], so this record uses the ordinary charge-separated resonance form C6H5-[N+](=O)-OH (charge on nitrogen) for the precursor. That is the same species; only the resonance form differs, and the difference is disclosed here rather than hidden. For the product the book's localization IS reproduced exactly: the charge sits on the oxygen that now carries both the phenyl and the hydrogen. ARROW-CHECK NOTE: this step's two moves are two-electron moves into and out of non-bonding orbitals, so the bookkeeping emits the expected soft 'consistent with a lone pair rather than radicals' advisories on atoms 7 and 8.

Equation 8.124, SECOND arrow, labelled with an italic 'i' (McLafferty's symbol for charge-site-induced, inductive cleavage), pointing at two printed products: a benzene ring bearing 'OH' with '+.' written above that oxygen and, after the plus sign, 'NO.'. So the O-N bond of the protonated phenyl nitrite is cleaved and the charge stays with the phenol. ARC COUNT (convention D): Book draws 0 arc(s) for this step - the middle structure carries no curly arrows at all; both moves <1,2> are curator-supplied. TENSION WITH THE 'i' LABEL, DISCLOSED: a strictly inductive (heterolytic) cleavage of an even-electron ion would send the O-N bonding pair to one fragment and give a closed-shell cation, e.g. neutral C6H5OH plus NO+. The products the book actually DRAWS are an odd-electron phenol radical cation and an NO radical, which can only arise by HOMOLYSIS of the O-N bond, so that is what is encoded: one fishhook leaves an electron on nitrogen (giving NO.) and the other leaves an electron on oxygen (giving the phenol radical cation whose '+.' the book prints on that very oxygen). This is the even-electron-rule violation the facing-page text describes when it says 'Loss of NO may also occur from aromatic EE+ ions'; the driving force it gives is 'the much-higher resonance stabilization of ArO+ than of Ar+' together with 'the large enthalpic advantage of ~2 eV for the rearrangement loss of NO vs. simple cleavage loss of NO2'. step_class is kept as 'inductive_cleavage' because that is the book's own label for the arrow.

NO MOD RULE IS CROSS-LINKED. rule_index.json 'by_equation' has no key '8.124' (chapter-8 keys stop at '8.14'), and no rule in the set expels NO or migrates an aryl group. Candidates CHECKED with RDKit against this record's own species (convention E): (i) the nitrogen rules IMS_4_43_ '[C]1..[C]5..[N+.]8([H]9)[C]10..[C]13..>>' and IMS_4_43_rH both require an N-H on a charged nitrogen; the query '[#6]-[#6]-[#7+](-[#1])-[#6]-[#6]' gives 0 matches on protonated nitrobenzene, whose [N+] carries two oxygens and an aryl, no hydrogen and no carbon chain. (ii) IMS_4_29, the only rule whose product is a neutral amine leaving group, needs '[N+](H)(H)C'; '[#7+](-[#1])(-[#1])-[#6]' gives 0 matches. (iii) The generic 'substituion' rule '[_A]1[C]2[C]3[_A+.]4>>[_A.]1.[C]2[C]3[_A+]4{-}2' needs an atom that is both charged and radical; the proxy skeleton query '[!#1]-[#6]-[#6]-[!#1+]' gives 0 matches on either the precursor or the nitrite intermediate, and neither species has any atom carrying both a charge and an unpaired electron. (iv) No rule in the set produces a radical cation from an even-electron ion, which is exactly what the second step of this equation does, so the whole scheme lies outside the current rule set.

NO MEASUREMENT ON THE PAGE (conventions F/G): equation 8.124 prints structures and the two reaction labels only; no m/z and no abundance appear either in the scheme or in the prose, which says merely that aromatic nitro compounds show 'characteristic (M - NO)+ ... peaks'. The product ion is therefore detected=false with status 'inferred' and no relative_intensity. 94.0408 is a curator-computed monoisotopic m/z (RDKit ExactMolWt of C6H6O, electron-mass corrected) for the phenol radical cation the book draws; the precursor [C6H5NO2 + H]+ is 124.0388 by the same computation and the neutral radical lost is NO. 29.9980. MS CONTEXT (convention G): the reacting species is a PROTONATED MOLECULE, not [M]+., so ionization_method is 'CI', adduct is '[M+H]+', precursor_mz is the m/z of [M+H]+, and electron_energy_ev is null - the cited work (Crombie and Harrison 1988) is a chemical-ionization study and the page states no electron energy.
